aiapget.eligibility: BAMS, BUMS, BSMS or BHMS with registration and internship completed by the cut-off date

aissee.body: National Testing Agency (NTA) for the Sainik Schools Society
aissee.pattern: Class 6: 125 MCQs, 300 marks (Language, Maths, Intelligence, GK). Class 9: 150 MCQs, 400 marks (Maths, Intelligence, English, Science, Social Science). No negative marking
aissee.age: Class 6: 10 to 12 years on 31 March of the admission year. Class 9: 13 to 15 years

links: DCECE(PE) 2026 round 1 opening and closing ranks (PDF)

cds.fee: ₹200; no fee for women and SC/ST candidates
cds.pattern: IMA, INA, AFA: English, GK and Elementary Maths, 100 marks each (300). OTA: English and GK only (200). One-third negative marking
cds.age: IMA and INA 19–24; AFA 20–24 (26 with a commercial pilot licence); OTA 19–25
cds.eligibility: IMA and OTA: any degree. INA: engineering degree or B.Sc with Physics and Maths. AFA: degree with Physics and Maths at Class 12, or B.E. Final-year students can apply
cds.attempts: Held twice a year; no attempt limit within the age band

cmat.pattern: 100 MCQs, 400 marks in 5 sections (Quant and DI, Logical Reasoning, Language, General Awareness, Innovation and Entrepreneurship). +4 correct, −1 wrong
cmat.eligibility: Bachelor's degree in any discipline (final-year students can apply)
links: CMAT 2026 answer key notice (exam held 25 Jan 2026)

csir-net.pattern: Parts A, B and C, 200 marks in every subject. Negative marking in most parts (varies by subject)
csir-net.age: JRF: up to 30 years on 1 Dec 2026 (up to 5 years' relaxation for OBC-NCL, SC, ST, PwD, third gender, women). No age limit for Assistant Professor or PhD
csir-net.attempts: No attempt limit; held twice a year

next.regText: 7 Oct – 5 Nov 2026 (late fee till 9 Nov); correction 10–12 Nov

links: Joint CSIR-UGC NET December 2026 information bulletin (PDF)

cuet-pg.fee: Up to 2 papers: ₹1,400 (General), ₹1,200 (EWS/OBC-NCL), ₹1,100 (SC/ST/third gender), ₹1,000 (PwBD); each extra paper ₹700 (General) or ₹600. Outside India ₹7,000. Up to 4 papers

cuet-ug.fee: Up to 3 subjects: ₹1,000 (General), ₹900 (OBC-NCL/EWS), ₹800 (SC/ST/PwBD/third gender); each extra subject ₹400 / ₹375 / ₹350. Outside India ₹4,500 (+₹1,800 per extra subject)
cuet-ug.pattern: 50 compulsory MCQs per test; +5 correct, −1 wrong. Up to 5 tests including languages and the General Aptitude Test
cuet-ug.age: No age limit for CUET itself; universities may have their own

gpat.body: National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) for the Pharmacy Council of India
gpat.eligibility: B.Pharm (final-year and pre-final-year students can apply)
gpat.attempts: One application per year; no limit across years stated

ies-ese.fee: ₹200; no fee for women, SC, ST and PwBD candidates
ies-ese.mode: Prelims: objective (OMR). Mains: written. Then personality test
ies-ese.duration: Prelims: Paper I 2 hours, Paper II 3 hours
ies-ese.pattern: Prelims 500 marks: Paper I General Studies and Engineering Aptitude (200), Paper II engineering discipline (300). One-third negative marking
ies-ese.age: 21 to 30 on 1 Jan 2027 (born 2 Jan 1997 – 1 Jan 2006). Relaxation: SC/ST 5 years, OBC 3, PwBD 10
ies-ese.eligibility: Engineering degree (or equivalent listed in the notice); final-year students can apply

jipmat.body: National Testing Agency (NTA) for IIM Bodh Gaya and IIM Jammu
jipmat.pattern: 100 MCQs, 400 marks: Quant 33, DI and LR 33, Verbal and RC 34. +4 correct, −1 wrong
jipmat.eligibility: Class 12 (any stream) passed in the last two years or appearing; Class 10 passed in or after the year set in the bulletin

nchm-jee.fee: ₹1,000 (General/OBC-NCL); ₹700 (EWS); ₹450 (SC/ST/PwD/third gender). GST and bank charges extra
nchm-jee.pattern: 120 MCQs: Numerical 15, Reasoning 15, GK 15, English 45, Service-sector aptitude 30. +4 correct, −1 wrong

nda.fee: ₹100; no fee for women, SC/ST, and wards of JCOs/NCOs/ORs at Sainik or Military Schools
nda.pattern: Maths 300 marks + General Ability Test 600 marks (English 200, GK 400) = 900; SSB 900. One-third negative marking
nda.age: About 16.5 to 19.5 years (NDA II 2026: born 1 Jan 2008 – 1 Jan 2011)
nda.eligibility: Unmarried men and women. Army wing: Class 12 any stream. Air Force, Navy and Naval Academy: Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Maths. Class 12 students can apply
nda.attempts: Held twice a year (April and September); no attempt limit within the age band

neet-ug.fee: ₹1,700 (General); ₹1,600 (EWS/OBC-NCL); ₹1,000 (SC/ST/PwBD/third gender); ₹9,500 outside India. GST and bank charges extra
neet-ug.pattern: 180 compulsory MCQs, 720 marks: Physics 45, Chemistry 45, Biology 90. +4 correct, −1 wrong
neet-ug.age: At least 17 by 31 Dec of the exam year; no upper limit
neet-ug.attempts: No attempt limit stated in the 2026 bulletin

ojee.fee: ₹1,000 for one course; ₹500 for each extra course
ojee.duration: 2 hours for most papers (1 hour for some)
ojee.pattern: MCQs: +4 for a correct answer, −1 for a wrong one
ojee.attempts: No limit stated in the 2026 brochure

rrb-alp.fee: ₹500 (₹400 refunded after CBT 1). SC, ST, ex-servicemen, women, transgender, minority and EBC: ₹250 (fully refunded after CBT 1)
rrb-alp.mode: Online CBT 1, CBT 2, then a computer-based aptitude test (CBAT)
rrb-alp.pattern: CBT 1: 75 questions (Maths, Mental Ability, General Science). CBT 2 Part A: 100 questions; Part B: 75 trade questions (qualifying at 35%). One-third negative marking. Final merit: CBT 2 Part A and CBAT, 50:50
rrb-alp.age: 18 to 30 on 1 Jul 2026. Relaxation: SC/ST 5 years, OBC 3
rrb-alp.eligibility: Class 10 plus ITI in a listed trade, or apprenticeship, or a diploma/degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Electronics or Automobile engineering

last.exam: CBT dates published on the RRB websites

rrb-group-d.fee: ₹500 (₹400 refunded after the CBT). SC, ST, ex-servicemen, PwBD, women, transgender, minority and EBC: ₹250 (fully refunded after the CBT)
rrb-group-d.mode: Online CBT, then physical efficiency test, documents and medical
rrb-group-d.pattern: 100 questions: General Science 25, Maths 25, Reasoning 30, General Awareness 20. One-third negative marking. PET: men carry 35 kg for 100 m and run 1,000 m in 4 min 15 s; women 20 kg and 1,000 m in 5 min 40 s
rrb-group-d.age: 18 to 33 on 1 Jan 2026. Relaxation: SC/ST 5 years, OBC 3, PwBD 10 to 15
rrb-group-d.eligibility: Class 10 or ITI (post-wise details in the notification)

last.exam: CBT dates published on the RRB websites

rrb-ntpc.fee: ₹500 (₹400 refunded after CBT 1). Concession categories ₹250 (fully refunded after CBT 1)
rrb-ntpc.mode: Online CBT 1, CBT 2, typing or aptitude test (some posts), documents and medical
rrb-ntpc.pattern: CBT 1: 100 questions (General Awareness 40, Maths 30, Reasoning 30). CBT 2: 120 questions. One-third negative marking
rrb-ntpc.age: Usually 18–30 (Class 12 posts) or 18–33/36 (graduate posts); check each CEN
rrb-ntpc.eligibility: Class 12 for undergraduate posts (clerks, typists); a degree for graduate posts (Station Master, Goods Guard and others)
links: Station Master recruitment 2026, 1,265 posts (press release, PDF)

ssc-cgl.fee: ₹100; no fee for women, SC, ST, PwBD and eligible ex-servicemen
ssc-cgl.mode: Online (CBT): Tier I, then Tier II
ssc-cgl.duration: Tier I: 1 hour (15-minute timer per section)
ssc-cgl.pattern: Tier I: 100 MCQs, 200 marks (Reasoning, General Awareness, Quant, English, 25 each). −0.5 per wrong answer
ssc-cgl.age: 18–27 or 18–30 on 1 Aug (depends on the post; 32 for Junior Statistical Officer), with relaxations
ssc-cgl.eligibility: Bachelor's degree (final-year students who finish by 1 Aug can apply). Some posts need Maths or Statistics

last.exam: Tier I: 30 Sep – 30 Oct 2026; Tier II: December 2026 (tentative)

ssc-chsl.fee: ₹100; no fee for women, SC, ST, PwBD and eligible ex-servicemen
ssc-chsl.mode: Online (CBT): Tier I, then Tier II
ssc-chsl.duration: Tier I: 60 minutes (15-minute timer per section)
ssc-chsl.pattern: Tier I: 100 MCQs, 200 marks (English, Reasoning, Quant, General Awareness, 25 each). −0.5 per wrong answer
ssc-chsl.age: 18 to 27 on 1 Aug 2026 (born 2 Aug 1999 – 1 Aug 2008). Relaxation: SC/ST 5 years, OBC 3, PwBD 10
ssc-chsl.eligibility: Class 12 pass (Science with Maths for some DEO posts)

ssc-cpo.fee: ₹100; no fee for women, SC, ST and eligible ex-servicemen
ssc-cpo.mode: Online (CBT) Paper I, physical tests, Paper II, medical
ssc-cpo.pattern: Paper I: 100 MCQs, 100 marks (Reasoning, GK, Quant, English, 25 each). −0.25 per wrong answer
ssc-cpo.age: 20 to 25 on 1 Aug 2026 (SI Fire, CISF: 18 to 30). Relaxation: SC/ST 5 years, OBC 3
ssc-cpo.eligibility: Bachelor's degree. Men applying for Delhi Police need a car and motorcycle licence. Height: men 170 cm, women 157 cm (relaxed for hill areas and ST)
links: SI in Delhi Police and CAPFs 2026 notice (PDF)

ssc-gd.fee: ₹100; no fee for women, SC, ST and eligible ex-servicemen
ssc-gd.mode: Online (CBT), then physical tests and medical
ssc-gd.pattern: 80 MCQs, 160 marks (Reasoning, GK, Elementary Maths, English/Hindi, 20 each). −0.25 per wrong answer. Paper in English, Hindi and 13 regional languages
ssc-gd.age: 18 to 23 on 1 Jan of the exam year. Relaxation: SC/ST 5 years, OBC 3
ssc-gd.eligibility: Class 10 pass, with domicile of the state chosen. Height: men 170 cm, women 157 cm (relaxed for some regions and ST). Run: men 5 km in 24 min, women 1.6 km in 8.5 min
links: SSC tentative calendar 2026–27 (GD 2027 notice planned for Sep 2026) (PDF)

ssc-je.fee: ₹100; no fee for women, SC, ST, PwBD and ex-servicemen
ssc-je.mode: Online (CBT): Paper I (qualifying), then Paper II
ssc-je.pattern: Paper I: 200 MCQs, 200 marks (Reasoning 50, General Awareness 50, engineering subject 100), −0.25 per wrong answer. Paper II: 100 questions, 300 marks, −1 per wrong answer
ssc-je.age: Up to 30 or 32 on 1 Aug 2026, depending on the post, with relaxations
ssc-je.eligibility: Diploma or degree in Civil, Mechanical or Electrical engineering (varies by post)

next.short: Paper I: 2–6 Nov and 30 Nov – 1 Dec 2026

last.exam: Paper I: 2–6 Nov and 30 Nov – 1 Dec 2026

ssc-mts.mode: Online (CBT) in two sessions; Havaldar posts also have physical tests

ssc-steno.fee: ₹100; no fee for women, SC, ST, PwBD and eligible ex-servicemen
ssc-steno.mode: Online (CBT), then a stenography skill test
ssc-steno.pattern: 200 MCQs, 200 marks (Reasoning 50, General Awareness 50, English 100). −0.25 per wrong answer. Skill test: dictation at 100 wpm (Grade C) or 80 wpm (Grade D)
ssc-steno.age: Grade C: 18–30; Grade D: 18–27 (on 1 Aug 2026), with relaxations

ts-polycet.body: State Board of Technical Education and Training (SBTET), Telangana
ts-polycet.eligibility: Passed or appearing Class 10 (SSC) or equivalent

last.reg: 2 Feb – 20 Apr 2026 (late fee till 21 Apr, tatkal till 22 Apr)

ugc-net.duration: 3 hours for both papers together, no break
ugc-net.pattern: Paper I: 50 MCQs (100 marks), teaching and research aptitude. Paper II: 100 MCQs (200 marks) in your subject. 2 marks each, no negative marking
ugc-net.age: JRF: up to 30 years on 1 Dec 2026 (up to 5 years' relaxation for OBC-NCL, SC, ST, PwD, third gender, women). No age limit for Assistant Professor or PhD
ugc-net.attempts: No attempt limit; held twice a year (June and December)

next.regText: 8 – 28 Oct 2026 (late fee till 31 Oct); correction 2–4 Nov

upsc-capf.fee: ₹200; no fee for women and SC/ST candidates
upsc-capf.mode: Written, then physical tests, interview and medical
upsc-capf.duration: Paper I 2 hours; Paper II 3 hours
upsc-capf.pattern: Paper I General Ability and Intelligence (250, objective, one-third negative marking). Paper II GS, Essay and Comprehension (200, written)
upsc-capf.age: 20 to 25 on 1 Aug of the exam year. Relaxation: SC/ST 5 years, OBC 3
upsc-capf.eligibility: Bachelor's degree; men and women. Physical standards apply (e.g. height 165 cm men, 157 cm women)

upsc-cse.fee: Prelims ₹100; Mains ₹200. No fee for women, SC, ST and PwBD candidates
upsc-cse.mode: Prelims: objective (OMR). Mains: written. Then personality test
upsc-cse.duration: Prelims: two papers of 2 hours each
upsc-cse.pattern: Prelims: GS Paper I (200 marks, counts for merit) and CSAT Paper II (200 marks, qualifying at 33%). One-third negative marking
upsc-cse.age: 21 to 32 on 1 Aug of the exam year. Relaxation: SC/ST 5 years, OBC 3, PwBD 10
upsc-cse.attempts: General/EWS 6; OBC 9; SC/ST no limit (within the age limit)
upsc-cse.eligibility: Bachelor's degree in any subject (final-year students can apply for prelims)

last.result: Prelims result 18 Jun 2026; Mains results announced on upsc.gov.in

upsc-geo.fee: ₹200; no fee for women, SC, ST and PwBD candidates
upsc-geo.mode: Prelims: objective (OMR). Mains: written. Then personality test
upsc-geo.duration: Prelims: two papers of 2 hours each
upsc-geo.pattern: Prelims 400 marks: Paper I General Studies (100), Paper II stream paper (300). One-third negative marking
upsc-geo.age: 21 to 32 on 1 Jan 2027 (born 2 Jan 1995 – 1 Jan 2006), with relaxations
upsc-geo.eligibility: Master's degree in Geology, Geophysics, Chemistry or Hydrogeology, depending on the post

upsc-ifos.fee: Prelims ₹100; Mains ₹200. No fee for women, SC, ST and PwBD candidates
upsc-ifos.mode: Prelims is the Civil Services prelims (one common form). Then IFoS Mains and interview
upsc-ifos.age: 21 to 32 on 1 Aug of the exam year, with relaxations
upsc-ifos.eligibility: Bachelor's degree with Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Science, Botany, Chemistry, Geology, Maths, Physics, Statistics or Zoology, or a degree in Agriculture, Forestry or Engineering

upsc-iss.fee: ₹200; no fee for women, SC, ST and PwBD candidates
upsc-iss.pattern: ISS: General English, General Studies, Statistics I–IV (I and II objective). IES: General English, General Studies, Economics I–III, Indian Economics
upsc-iss.age: 21 to 30 on 1 Aug of the exam year, with relaxations
upsc-iss.eligibility: ISS: bachelor's with Statistics (or master's in Statistics). IES: master's in Economics, Applied, Business Economics or Econometrics

wbjee.duration: Two papers of 2 hours each (Maths; Physics and Chemistry)
wbjee.pattern: Maths 75 MCQs (100 marks); Physics 40 and Chemistry 40 MCQs (50 marks each). Wrong answers lose ¼ of the marks in single-answer questions; no negative marking in multi-correct questions
wbjee.age: At least 17 years by 31 Dec of the exam year; no upper limit (25 for Marine Engineering)
wbjee.attempts: No attempt limit stated in the 2026 bulletin
wbjee.eligibility: Class 12 with Physics and Maths plus Chemistry or another listed subject, 45% in these (40% reserved) and 30% in English
